headline: The Oakland County Homeowner's Complete Guide to Spring Fence Installation in 2026
description: Everything Oakland County homeowners need to know about installing a wood fence this spring — from permits and materials to costs, timelines, and why April is the perfect time to start.

mainEntity.name: How much does a privacy fence cost in Oakland County, Michigan in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 6-foot cedar privacy fence costs $35-55 per linear foot installed. For an average backyard of 200 linear feet, expect $7,000-$11,000. Pressure-treated pine runs $25-40 per linear foot, or $5,000-$8,000 for the same 200-foot perimeter.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to build a fence in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most cities and villages in Oakland County — Auburn Hills, Rochester, Troy, Bloomfield Hills, Pontiac, Lake Orion — require a permit. Oakland County itself does not have a county-wide permit, but individual municipalities do. BF Fence handles all permit applications as part of our installation service.

mainEntity.name: What is the best wood for a fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Western red cedar is the best wood for Michigan fence installations. Its natural oils resist rot, insects, and moisture. Cedar fences last 15-25 years with minimal maintenance. Pressure-treated pine is a budget alternative that lasts 10-15 years with diligent re-sealing every 2-3 years.

mainEntity.name: How deep should fence posts be in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fence posts should be set a minimum of 42 inches below grade — Michigan's frost line depth. In areas prone to frost heave, 48 inches is recommended. Posts should be set in a 10-12 inch hole with a gravel base, high-strength concrete, and proper bracing.

mainEntity.name: Should I stain or seal my new fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Pressure-treated pine needs to dry for 4-6 weeks before staining. Cedar can be sealed at installation or within the first year. Oil-based semi-transparent stain is recommended for the best balance of protection and natural wood appearance.

mainEntity.name: How long does fence installation take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical residential fence installation (150-250 linear feet) takes 2-5 working days. Larger projects or installations requiring old fence removal can extend to 7-10 days.
